main_issue: Who will complete Agent D's section of the Thursday pitch after D's grandmother's death; A takes it over, B and C decline, D agrees and briefs A.

A-B.evidence: B said they can't take on more (turn 4); A took over the section (turn 7). B never addressed A or the arrangement; A noted a 'tight spot' (turn 3).

A-C.evidence: C declined to help (turn 5), then thanked A: 'That's a big help' (turn 11), endorsing A's takeover.

A-D.evidence: D first proposed working evenings (turn 6); A said 'that's not right' and offered to take over (turn 7). D accepted and briefed A (turns 8-27).

B-C.evidence: Both declined to take on more work (turns 4, 5); neither addressed the other, and B stayed silent after A's takeover while C endorsed it.

B-D.evidence: B said they can't take on more (turn 4); D said 'I understand' (turn 6), but B never took a position on the final arrangement.

C-D.evidence: D answered C's refusal with 'I understand' (turn 6); C later welcomed A's takeover (turn 11), which D also accepted.
